method: Three fresh implicit, unfunded NEAR wallets in each sequential baseline, concurrent dispatch, and restored control arm. The same SDK assets, browser harness and client machine run all arms. Router, Deriver A and Deriver B change together. Signing Worker, Gateway, Runtime, Console and placement settings stay fixed.

independentSignatureVerification.verifier: Node.js crypto Ed25519 with independent NEP-413 Borsh encoding

limitations: Three samples per arm do not establish tail percentiles or a latency guarantee.
Sequential arms include provider scheduling and network variation.
Fresh wallets do not prove cold Workers. Worker cold starts were not controlled.
Span start times derive from log time minus duration. A Worker clock advances only at I/O.
Nested spans overlap. Protocol spans include transport. Concurrent durations must not be added.
Bound-root D1 counters cover a subset of database work. Total registration D1 calls remain unmeasured.
Peer frame counts are not instrumented in hosted traces.
Requested APAC placement does not prove physical colocation.

decision.reason: The Router dispatches Deriver A with Deriver B instead of after B has prepared. Every hosted sample shows the dispatch and the overlap, and every candidate Yao execution is faster than every baseline and control sample.
decision.uncertainty: Three sequential samples per arm on one client. Worker cold state, provider scheduling and network conditions were not controlled. The first arm was the slowest in full-flow terms, so the baseline difference includes run order. Tail percentiles are not established.
notRecorded: Peer frame counts: hosted traces do not count frames.
decision.deployment: The measured versions are not served. Staging runs its original versions.
